name: MMseqs2, three rounds
kind: builds a profile of a protein family
compares: A profile of a protein family, built by MMseqs2 from its own hits over three rounds of search, as jackhmmer does.
reference: The relative's proteome (Quest for Orthologs reference proteomes, release 2020_04), as an MMseqs2 database.
score: Bit score: higher ranks first. The E-value cutoff was 10.
failure_modes: At most 1,000 target proteins are kept per query (--max-seqs 1000). How often that cut hits: not measured.
Each round can pull in proteins from a different family. How often: not measured.
command:
mmseqs search \
    human-38fdd87d_mmdb/db zebrafish_mmdb/db result mmseqs_tmp \
    --threads 16 \
    -s 7 \
    --num-iterations 3 \
    --max-seqs 1000 \
    -e 10.0
questions: Is the closest same-family domain in the relative you will search at least 40% identical, for most of your proteins? If yes, Fmax here is 40–60% 0.241 (n = 563), 60–100% 0.300 (n = 1,289). If no, 20–30% 0.337 (n = 93), 30–40% 0.209 (n = 165). (Pfam truth set, raw calls, zebrafish (435 Mya) as the relative searched, setting sensitivity 7, 3 rounds; subsets with at least 30 true instances.)

Are the features you care about longer than 60 residues? If yes, Fmax here is 61–120 aa 0.245 (n = 963), 121–250 aa 0.319 (n = 504), 251 aa or more 0.462 (n = 277). If no, 16–30 aa 0.028 (n = 271), 31–60 aa 0.085 (n = 420). (Pfam truth set, raw calls, zebrafish (435 Mya) as the relative searched, setting sensitivity 7, 3 rounds.)
Can you spend about 0.0787 core-hours per 1,000 proteins for each relative you search? That is the measured mean per relative; see "Cost per 1,000 queries" below.
